problem: Given that the expression $4\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ)$ with $R>0,$ what is the value of $R?$

activity_context.topic_title: Writing Sums of Trigonometric Functions in Amplitude-Phase Form

feedback.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
6\operatorname{sin}⁡x+8\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
6\operatorname{sin}⁡x+8\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=6 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=8\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={6}^{2}+{8}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =36+64 \\ {R}^{2} & =100 \\ R & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$
